claim: Open table formats (Apache Iceberg) prevent proprietary vendor lock-in and enable zero data copy across analytical engines.
description: IOMETE is architected natively around Apache Iceberg open table formats and Parquet files stored directly in customer-owned object storage (S3, GCS, Azure Blob, or MinIO/Ceph on-prem). Data remains in standard open formats accessible by any Iceberg-compliant engine without extraction or vendor egress penalties.
qualification_or_limitation: Requires migration or in-place registration of existing data files into Apache Iceberg table format; requires underlying object storage infrastructure.

claim: Complete Data Sovereignty: Data and compute reside entirely inside the customer's own cloud VPC or on-premises data centre.
description: Unlike multi-tenant SaaS platforms where data or query metadata leaves customer perimeters, IOMETE installs directly into the customer's Kubernetes environment (EKS, GKE, AKS, OpenShift, or bare-metal Kubernetes). The control plane can also run self-hosted or air-gapped, ensuring sensitive data never crosses external network boundaries.
source_title: Self-Hosted Data Platform & Private Cloud Architecture
qualification_or_limitation: Customer is responsible for providing and maintaining the underlying Kubernetes infrastructure and object storage resources.

claim: Proven on-premises Lakehouse reference architecture for highly regulated banking and financial institutions.
description: IOMETE provides a validated deployment pattern for tier-1 financial institutions requiring strict regulatory compliance, network isolation (air-gapped/on-premises bare metal), and strict data residency without compromising modern SQL analytics or Spark workloads.
source_title: On-Premises Lakehouse Reference Architecture for Banks
qualification_or_limitation: Hardware sizing, SAN/NAS/MinIO performance, and local high-availability topologies must be reviewed during technical discovery.

claim: Predictable workload-based compute economics without proprietary query markup or hidden egress overhead.
description: IOMETE separates compute from storage and utilizes isolated, autoscaling Apache Spark clusters per department or workload. Because users run clusters on their own negotiated cloud/hardware compute instances, they avoid the 3x-5x credit markup typical of proprietary SaaS data warehouses.
source_title: IOMETE Design Principles: Compute & Storage Decoupling
qualification_or_limitation: Actual financial savings depend on workload concurrency, cluster utilization efficiency, and baseline cloud discounting vs. current Snowflake/Databricks commitments.

claim: Enterprise-grade fine-grained access control (RBAC), row/column masking, and Apache Ranger integration.
description: Unified governance engine providing column-level masking, row-level filtering, tag-based policies, and comprehensive audit logging across all SQL and programmatic Spark queries.
qualification_or_limitation: Active Directory/LDAP/Okta identity provider integration requires configuration during initial onboarding.

claim: Sovereign Lakehouse Proof at Scale: High-throughput ingestion and sub-second BI query acceleration over Iceberg metadata.
description: Optimized Spark query engine combined with Iceberg metadata indexing and file pruning delivers interactive SQL performance for BI tools (PowerBI, Tableau, Superset) while handling petabyte-scale batch pipelines.
qualification_or_limitation: Interactive sub-second query performance on complex joins requires appropriate cluster sizing and partitioning strategies.

claim: Coexistence and phased migration: IOMETE can query existing object storage and operate alongside Snowflake/Databricks without rip-and-replace.
description: Because IOMETE runs on open formats, enterprises can register existing Parquet/Iceberg datasets and run specific high-cost or data-sensitive workloads on IOMETE while maintaining existing BI dashboards and upstream pipelines.
qualification_or_limitation: Proprietary Snowflake-specific SQL dialect scripts or stored procedures require compatibility mapping before migration.

claim: Unified Lakehouse foundation for Generative AI and ML workloads without data movement.
description: Direct Python, PySpark, and notebook integration with Iceberg tables allows data science and ML engineering teams to train and fine-tune models directly within the secure perimeter without extracting data into third-party vector or feature stores.
qualification_or_limitation: GPU scheduling requires Kubernetes cluster nodes configured with compatible NVIDIA drivers.
